headline: Ferries and Victorian Lodging Logistics
reservation: Access to the island requires a ferry ticket, while the island itself is a state park with no entry fee. The bottleneck is overnight accommodation; Victorian hotels and B&Bs often book a year in advance for summer weekends. Ferry schedules vary by season and weather; check official operators like Shepler's or Star Line for current departures.

days.title: Coastal Perimeter and Harbor Life
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Mackinaw City Ferry Dock

stops.name: M-185 Shoreline Loop
stops.detail: Cycle the only motor-free state highway in the US, an 8-mile paved path encircling the island.

stops.name: Arch Rock
stops.detail: View the 146-foot natural limestone span from the shoreline road and the upper bluff stairs.

days.driving: Local transfer by ferry (20 mins) followed by walking or cycling.
days.note: Bicycle rentals are high-volume; arriving before 10 AM ensures the best selection of specialized equipment.

days.title: Fortifications and Interior Forests

stops.name: Fort Mackinac
stops.detail: Explore the 14 original historic buildings and watch live rifle demonstrations overlooking the Straits.

stops.name: Sugar Loaf
stops.detail: Hike to this 75-foot limestone breccia stack located in the island's wooded interior.

days.driving: No motorized vehicles; allow time for horse-drawn taxi transit if not walking.
days.note: The walk to the fort is a steep uphill climb; horse carriages are available for those with mobility concerns.

days.title: High Bluffs and Historic Homes

stops.name: Biddle House
stops.detail: Learn about the island's fur trading history at one of the oldest residential structures in Michigan.

stops.name: Grand Hotel West Bluff
stops.detail: Stroll past the iconic Victorian cottages for views of the Mackinac Bridge.

days.driving: Walking or horse-drawn carriage; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: Non-guest access to the Grand Hotel porch typically requires a separate admission fee.

intel.title: Ferry Weather Impacts
intel.text: High winds on Lake Huron can cause ferry delays or cancellations. Monitor the official ferry social media channels for real-time straits conditions.

intel.title: Mainland Refueling
intel.text: Fuel is only available in Mackinaw City or St. Ignace before boarding the ferry. There are no gas stations for public use on the island.

intel.title: Downtown Connectivity
intel.text: Signal is generally strong in the harbor area but can drop in the interior cedar forests. Download offline maps for the 70 miles of interior trails.

intel.title: Day Tripper Flux
intel.text: The island is quietest before 10 AM and after 5 PM. Plan your Main Street shopping outside of the peak ferry arrival window.

intel.title: Mainland Staging
intel.text: Large secure parking lots are available at the ferry terminals in Mackinaw City. Overnight guests should utilize the designated long-term valet or shuttle lots.

plan.arrival: Fly into Pellston (PLN), take a shuttle to Mackinaw City, and board the ferry; your luggage is typically transferred directly to island hotels.
plan.vehicle: Cars are prohibited on the island; leave your vehicle in a secure mainland ferry lot.
plan.goldenHour: The West Bluff offers elevated views of the Mackinac Bridge at sunset, subject to evening cloud cover.
